_comment: eval/gen_cases.json — the generation eval set (HW5, T14.14). Owner: Dias.
It EXTENDS eval/cases.json rather than duplicating it. `extends` names the base
set; the 24 cases there are loaded first and the `cases` below are appended, for
30 in total. Two reasons for extending and not starting again. First, Parts 2 and
3 then describe the SAME queries, so 'the retrieval metrics went up and the answer
metrics did not' is a statement about one system rather than a comparison of two
unrelated question sets — which is the whole of Part 4. Second, a golden ANSWER is
already written for every base case; a separate generation set would have meant
writing 20 more of them and would have measured a different corpus of questions.
The six added here are questions the retrieval metrics cannot fail on but a
generator can: the corpus contains material that pulls the wrong way (g01, g03),
a measured number that invites invention (g02), two concepts that are easy to
conflate (g04), an error branch that is easy to state backwards (g05), and a
second out-of-corpus question that sounds far more answerable than the base set's
kubernetes/lambda pair (g06). Categories stay inside the seven the base set uses,
so the per-category tables in Parts 2 and 3 line up row for row.
`rerank_off_subset` is the subset the reranking-OFF run scores. Judged metrics
cost an LLM call each, so the second run is a subset by design (assignment Part 3)
— but a RANDOM subset can drop a whole failure category, and the per-category
breakdown is the point. So it is stratified: two cases from each of the seven
categories, 14 in all, keeping every category present on both sides of the
comparison. Within a category the two are the lowest-numbered, so the choice is
not a post-hoc pick of the cases that made reranking look good.

cases.query: we run Postgres now, so should the sqlite overlay move into it
cases.golden_answer: No. The Postgres index is derived data that may be dropped and rebuilt, while the overlay is authored knowledge, so consolidating them would put durable records in a store the project treats as disposable. The overlay stays in sqlite under store/.

cases.query: how much slower is a search with reranking turned on
cases.golden_answer: About 4 seconds against roughly 60 milliseconds without it, a factor of about 60. Cached it drops to 60-140ms, which is why the eval harness can re-run the sweep for free while a live agent turn cannot.

cases.query: which tools need a human to approve them and which do not
cases.golden_answer: Only the irreversible one is gated: prune_graph_node proceeds solely on explicit human confirmation. The read tools, the append-only decision log and the scan stay ungated, because reversibility decides the gate rather than importance.

cases.query: what is the difference between a stale summary card and an orphaned decision
cases.golden_answer: A stale card is a summary whose source file changed, so the card describes code that has moved on and should be regenerated. An orphan is a record whose symbol_uid no longer resolves at all, which is surfaced for review and never deleted. Different signals with different fixes.

cases.query: what happens to search if the embeddings endpoint is unreachable
cases.golden_answer: The dense arm is dropped and the search degrades to lexical-only rather than failing: BM25 still runs over the same corpus and the hit records that it had no dense score, so a run that quietly lost an arm is visible in the trace instead of looking like a bad day for the retriever.
